The Sayyids were founded by Khizr Khan, Timur's nominee, after Timur's invasion of 1398 weakened the Tughlaqs. The Lodi dynasty, the only Afghan dynasty of the Sultanate, ended when Ibrahim Lodi was defeated at Panipat in 1526.

questions.question:
[Q.120 · Art & Culture]
Match List-I (Musician) with List-II (Instrument):
List-I
a. Bismillah Khan
b. Hariprasad Chaurasia
c. Zakir Hussain
d. Amjad Ali Khan
List-II
1. Sarod
2. Tabla
3. Shehnai
4. Flute (bansuri)
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Bismillah Khan – shehnai, Hariprasad Chaurasia – bansuri, Zakir Hussain – tabla and Amjad Ali Khan – sarod, so the code is a-3, b-4, c-2, d-1. Ustad Bismillah Khan was born at Dumraon (Buxar district, Bihar) and received the Bharat Ratna in 2001. Amjad Ali Khan belongs to the Senia Bangash gharana of sarod players.

questions.question:
[Q.121 · Art & Culture]
The Kangra school of Pahari painting reached its peak under the patronage of
questions.explanation: Raja Sansar Chand Katoch (r. 1775–1823) of Kangra was the great patron of the Kangra style, known for lyrical themes from the Gita Govinda and the Bhagavata Purana and for soft, graceful figures. Maharaja Serfoji II of Thanjavur is linked to Tanjore painting, and Raja Savant Singh of Kishangarh (Rajasthani school) to the Bani Thani style. Basohli and Guler are other centres of Pahari painting.

questions.question:
[Q.122 · Bihar]
Which ruler of the Haryanka dynasty shifted the capital of Magadha from Rajagriha to Pataliputra?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Udayin (Udayabhadra), son of Ajatashatru, founded the city of Pataliputra at the confluence of the Ganga and the Son and made it the capital. Ajatashatru had only built a fort at the village of Pataligrama to fight the Vajjis. Bimbisara, the founder of Haryanka power, ruled from Girivraja/Rajagriha, and the Shishunagas later moved the capital to Vaishali for a time.

questions.question:
[Q.123 · Bihar]
Consider the following statements about Nalanda:
1. The Nalanda mahavihara was founded in the reign of the Gupta ruler Kumaragupta I.
2. The archaeological site of Nalanda Mahavihara was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2014.
3. The new Nalanda University was set up under an Act of Parliament passed in 2010 and began classes in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. Nalanda was founded in the 5th century CE under Kumaragupta I (Shakraditya) and later patronised by Harsha and the Palas; it was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji around 1200 CE. Statement 2 is wrong: the site became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2016, not 2014. The Nalanda University Act, 2010 set up the new university near Rajgir, which started its first session in September 2014.

questions.question:
[Q.124 · Bihar]
Match List-I (Craft of Bihar) with List-II (Description):
List-I
a. Sujini
b. Sikki
c. Khatwa
d. Manjusha
List-II
1. Appliqué work, cut cloth stitched on a base fabric
2. Scroll-like painting on the Bihula–Vishahari legend
3. Quilted embroidery, associated with Muzaffarpur
4. Articles woven from golden grass
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
questions.explanation: Sujini is quilted embroidery from Muzaffarpur (GI tagged), Sikki items are woven from the golden grass found in Mithila (Madhubani, Sitamarhi, Darbhanga), Khatwa is appliqué work used on canopies and tents, and Manjusha art of Bhagalpur tells the story of Bihula and the snake goddess Vishahari. So the code is a-3, b-4, c-1, d-2. Sujini, Sikki and Manjusha all carry GI tags.

questions.question:
[Q.125 · General Mental Ability]
In a certain code, MANGO is written as 13114715, each letter being replaced by its position in the English alphabet. How will LEMON be written in that code?
questions.explanation: L = 12, E = 5, M = 13, O = 15, N = 14, so LEMON = 12-5-13-15-14 = 125131514. Check with the given word: M = 13, A = 1, N = 14, G = 7, O = 15 gives 13114715. Option B swaps O and N.

questions.question:
[Q.126 · General Mental Ability]
Find the wrong number in the series:
2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 64
questions.explanation: The terms are n² + 1 for n = 1, 2, 3, …: 2, 5, 10, 17, 26, 37, 50, 65. So the last term should be 65 (8² + 1), not 64. Another way: the differences are 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13 and then 15, so 50 + 15 = 65.

A − B: A is the wife of B. B + C: B is the father of C. C × D: C is the brother of D, so D is also a child of B. A is the wife of B, the father of D, so A is the mother of D. D's gender is not needed; the answer is the same either way.

questions.question:
[Q.128 · General Mental Ability]
Six friends A, B, C, D, E and F are sitting around a circular table facing the centre. A sits opposite D. B sits second to the right of A. E sits immediately to the right of D. F is not an immediate neighbour of E. Who sits opposite F?
questions.explanation: Place A at seat 1 and number the seats so that the right of each person comes next. D is opposite A at seat 4, B is second to A's right, and E is to D's immediate right. That leaves C and F for the two seats next to A; the seat next to E must be C because F cannot be beside E. The arrangement (anticlockwise from A) is A, C, E, D, B, F, which is unique, and E sits opposite F.

questions.question:
[Q.129 · General Mental Ability]
Which of the following best represents the relationship among the classes Doctors, Women and Mothers?
options: Three separate circles that do not touch
Three circles one inside the other
A circle for Mothers inside a circle for Women, with a circle for Doctors cutting across both
A circle for Women inside a circle for Mothers, with a circle for Doctors separate from both
questions.explanation: All mothers are women, so the Mothers circle lies inside the Women circle. Some doctors are women and some doctors are mothers, while some are neither (men), so the Doctors circle overlaps both. Option D wrongly puts Women inside Mothers.

questions.question:
[Q.130 · General Mental Ability]
If the English alphabet is written in reverse order (Z to A), which letter will be the 7th to the right of the 12th letter from the left?
questions.explanation: In the reversed alphabet, the 12th letter from the left is the 12th from Z, i.e. O (27 − 12 = 15). The 7th to its right is the 19th from the left in the reversed order, i.e. the letter at normal position 27 − 19 = 8, which is H. S is the answer if the order is not reversed (12 + 7 = 19th letter).

questions.question:
[Q.131 · General Mental Ability]
Statement: An advertisement says, 'Use our fluoride toothpaste to protect your teeth from decay.'
Assumptions:
I. People want to protect their teeth from decay.
II. No other toothpaste contains fluoride.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit?
options: Both I and II are implicit
Neither I nor II is implicit
questions.explanation: An advertisement promising protection from decay assumes that people care about it, so I is implicit. II is not implicit: the advertiser claims only that its product contains fluoride, not that other brands lack it. Advertisements assume a demand for the benefit offered, not the absence of competitors.

questions.question:
[Q.132 · General Mental Ability]
In how many different ways can the letters of the word PATNA be arranged?
questions.explanation: PATNA has 5 letters in which A occurs twice. Number of arrangements = 5! / 2! = 120 / 2 = 60. Option 120 ignores the repeated A.

questions.question:
[Q.133 · Arithmetic/Maths]
What is the sum of the first 20 terms of the arithmetic progression 5, 9, 13, 17, …?
questions.explanation: Here a = 5 and d = 4. S₂₀ = (20/2) × [2 × 5 + (20 − 1) × 4] = 10 × (10 + 76) = 860. The 20th term is 5 + 19 × 4 = 81, and S = 20 × (5 + 81) / 2 = 860 confirms it. 820 is the slip of using 18 instead of 19 for (n − 1): 10 × (10 + 72) = 820.

questions.question:
[Q.134 · Arithmetic/Maths]
A farmer gave 1/3 of his land to his wife and 1/2 of the remaining land to his son. The rest was divided equally between his two daughters, each of whom got 5 acres. How much land did the farmer have?
questions.explanation: After the wife's share, 2/3 of the land remains; the son gets half of it, i.e. 1/3, leaving 1/3 for the daughters. Each daughter gets 1/6 of the land, so 1/6 of the total = 5 acres and the total = 30 acres. Check: wife 10, son 10, daughters 5 + 5 = 30.

questions.question:
[Q.135 · Bihar]
The final electoral roll of Bihar, published on 30 September 2025 after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted by the Election Commission of India, contained about how many electors?
questions.explanation: The final roll had about 7.42 crore electors. The roll stood at about 7.89 crore on 24 June 2025 when the SIR began, the draft roll of 1 August 2025 had about 7.24 crore after some 65 lakh names were removed, and about 21.5 lakh names were added before the final roll. Bihar's SIR was the first such intensive revision in the state since 2003, and the exercise was later extended to other states.

questions.question:
[Q.136 · Bihar]
Nitin Nabin, a five-time MLA from Bihar, took charge in January 2026 as
options: National General Secretary (Organisation) of the BJP
National President of the BJP Yuva Morcha
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Nitin Nabin was elected unopposed and took charge as BJP National President on 20 January 2026, succeeding J.P. Nadda; at 45 he is the youngest person to hold the post. He had been appointed National Working President on 14 December 2025. He represents the Bankipur seat of Patna.

questions.question:
[Q.137 · Bihar]
Cricketer Vaibhav Suryavanshi, who received the Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar from President Droupadi Murmu in December 2025, belongs to which district of Bihar?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Vaibhav Suryavanshi is from Samastipur. He received the award (for children aged 5–18) at the Veer Baal Diwas function on 26 December 2025 in the sports category. In IPL 2025, aged 14, he scored a 35-ball century for Rajasthan Royals, the youngest centurion in T20 cricket and the fastest by an Indian in the IPL.

questions.question:
[Q.138 · Bihar]
The 2,400 MW (3 × 800 MW) thermal power project at Pirpainti, for which a 25-year power supply agreement was signed with the Bihar government in September 2025, is located in which district and is being developed by which company?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Pirpainti is in Bhagalpur district, and Adani Power won the project through tariff-based bidding (about ₹6.075 per kWh) on a design, build, finance, own and operate basis; the power supply agreement with Bihar's discoms was signed in September 2025. NTPC's older Kahalgaon super thermal power station is also in Bhagalpur district, which makes A a tempting distractor. Barauni (Begusarai) is another major thermal station in the state.

questions.question:
[Q.139 · Bihar]
Who was elected Speaker of the 18th Bihar Legislative Assembly on 2 December 2025?
questions.explanation: Senior BJP leader Dr Prem Kumar, MLA from Gaya Town, was elected Speaker unopposed on 2 December 2025. Narendra Narayan Yadav (JD(U)) was the pro-tem Speaker who conducted the election, and Nand Kishore Yadav was Speaker of the 17th Assembly from February 2024. Awadh Bihari Choudhary was Speaker from 2022 to 2024.

questions.question:
[Q.140 · Current Affairs (National)]
Consider the following statements about the Republic Day celebrations of 2026:
1. The chief guests were the President of the European Council, António Costa, and the President of the European Commission, Ursula von der Leyen.
2. It was the first time that more than one foreign leader was chief guest at a Republic Day parade.
3. The two leaders co-chaired the 16th India–EU Summit in New Delhi on 27 January 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: the two EU leaders were joint chief guests at the 77th Republic Day and co-chaired the India–EU Summit the next day. Statement 2 is wrong: in 2018 the heads of all ten ASEAN countries were chief guests together. The 2026 celebrations had '150 years of Vande Mataram' as their theme.

questions.question:
[Q.141 · Current Affairs (National)]
In September 2025, DRDO and the Strategic Forces Command carried out the first launch of which missile from a rail-based mobile launcher?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Agni-Prime (Agni-P), a two-stage solid-fuel, canisterised missile with a range of up to about 2,000 km, was test-fired from a specially designed rail-based launcher on 24 September 2025. The launcher can move on the normal rail network without pre-conditions, putting India among a few countries with this capability. A road-mobile version of Agni-Prime had already been inducted.

questions.question:
[Q.142 · Current Affairs (National)]
Who won the FIDE Chess World Cup 2025, held in Goa in November 2025?
questions.explanation: Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov, aged 19, beat China's Wei Yi in the rapid tiebreaks of the final on 26 November 2025, becoming the youngest winner of the World Cup. Andrey Esipenko finished third, and the top three qualified for the 2026 Candidates tournament. Sindarov beat his compatriot Nodirbek Yakubboev in the semi-final.

questions.question:
[Q.143 · Current Affairs (National)]
Which writer was chosen for the Sahitya Akademi Award 2025 in Hindi (announced in March 2026)?
questions.explanation: Mamta Kalia was chosen for her memoir 'Jeete Jee Allahabad'; the Akademi announced the 2025 awards in 24 languages on 16 March 2026 after a delay from December 2025. Gagan Gill won the Hindi award for 2024 (Main Jab Tak Aayi Bahar), Sanjeev for 2023 and Badri Narayan for 2022. The award carries ₹1 lakh and a copper plaque.

questions.question:
[Q.144 · Miscellaneous]
The Mother Tongue Survey of India, which completed field videography of 576 mother tongues, was carried out under which Union Ministry?
questions.explanation: The survey was run by the Language Division of the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, which comes under the Ministry of Home Affairs; the MHA annual report for 2021–22 reported its completion. It documents mother tongues returned in two or more censuses, and the recordings are to be archived on an NIC server. The Census is also conducted by the Registrar General under the MHA.

questions.question:
[Q.145 · Current Affairs (International)]
Under the arrangement agreed at COP30 in Belém, COP31 (November 2026) is being hosted by Türkiye in Antalya. Which country holds the role of 'President of Negotiations' for COP31?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Türkiye (COP31 President Murat Kurum) hosts the summit in Antalya and leads the action agenda, while Australia (Chris Bowen) is President of Negotiations; a pre-COP is to be held in a Pacific island country. It is the first UN climate summit with presidency powers split between two countries. Brazil presided over COP30.

questions.question:
[Q.146 · Current Affairs (International)]
Which one of the following sports was NOT part of the programme of the 2026 Commonwealth Games held at Glasgow?
questions.explanation: Glasgow 2026 (23 July–2 August 2026) had a slimmed-down programme of 10 sports, dropping wrestling, hockey, cricket, badminton, table tennis, squash and shooting. Boxing, weightlifting, judo, athletics, swimming, gymnastics, track cycling, netball, bowls and 3x3 basketball were held. India won 39 medals (13 gold) and finished fourth, with boxing its best sport.

questions.question:
[Q.147 · Current Affairs (International)]
Consider the following statements about the Global Innovation Index 2025 released by WIPO:
1. India was ranked 38th among 139 economies.
2. Switzerland was ranked first.
3. India entered the top 25 economies for the first time.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: India moved up from 39th (2024) to 38th in GII 2025, and Switzerland stayed top, followed by Sweden, the USA, South Korea and Singapore. Statement 3 is wrong since India is 38th, not in the top 25. WIPO lists India as the top economy in the lower-middle-income group.

questions.question:

By winning the Australian Open men's singles title in February 2026, who completed a career Grand Slam?
options: More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Carlos Alcaraz beat Novak Djokovic in the final; the Australian Open was the only major he had not yet won, so he completed the career Grand Slam. The women's title went to Elena Rybakina of Kazakhstan, who beat Aryna Sabalenka. Sinner had won the Australian Open in 2024 and 2025.

questions.question:
[Q.149 · Current Affairs (International)]
José Antonio Kast, who won the December 2025 run-off against Jeannette Jara, was sworn in on 11 March 2026 as the President of which country?
questions.explanation: Kast, a right-wing leader of the Republican Party, was sworn in as President of Chile at the National Congress in Valparaíso, succeeding Gabriel Boric. He defeated the communist candidate Jeannette Jara in the run-off. Argentina's president is Javier Milei.

questions.question:
[Q.150 · Current Affairs (International)]
China launched the Shenzhou-22 spacecraft without a crew in November 2025. What was the main reason?
options: To carry the first foreign astronaut to the Tiangong station
To give the Tiangong crew a safe return vehicle after a docked Shenzhou capsule's window was cracked, probably by space debris
To test a crewed lunar landing module
More than one of the above
questions.explanation: Cracks found in the window of Shenzhou-20 made it unsafe, so the Shenzhou-20 crew came home on 14 November 2025 in the Shenzhou-21 capsule, leaving the newly arrived Shenzhou-21 crew without a lifeboat. Shenzhou-22 was launched uncrewed on 25 November 2025 (Beijing time) to fill that gap, the first emergency launch of its kind for China. Shenzhou-21 (launched 31 October 2025) was also the first to reach Tiangong by a fast 3.5-hour rendezvous.
